meta.note: Rules are data. Add an entry here, register a check function with the same id, and the engine picks it up.

rules.title: Plaintext administrative protocol exposed
rules.why: Telnet and FTP send credentials and session data in clear text. Anyone on the same network segment can read them with a passive capture.
rules.remediation: Disable telnet/ftp. Use SSH/SFTP, or tunnel the service inside an authenticated, encrypted channel.

rules.title: HTTP response missing hardening headers
rules.why: Without CSP, X-Frame-Options, X-Content-Type-Options and Referrer-Policy the browser has no defence in depth against injected script, clickjacking and MIME sniffing.
rules.remediation: Set Content-Security-Policy, X-Frame-Options: DENY, X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff, Referrer-Policy: no-referrer; add Strict-Transport-Security once TLS is in place.

rules.title: Verbose server banner discloses product version
rules.why: An exact product and version in the Server header lets an attacker match the host against public advisories without any probing.
rules.remediation: Return a generic Server header (or none), move version detail to internal logs only.

rules.title: Weak TLS configuration
rules.why: TLS 1.0/1.1 and export or NULL ciphers are deprecated and breakable; they also fail modern compliance baselines.
rules.remediation: Allow only TLS 1.2+ with AEAD cipher suites (AES-GCM / ChaCha20-Poly1305), and disable renegotiation.

rules.title: Administrative path reachable without authentication
rules.why: An /admin surface answering 200 to an anonymous request means the control plane is exposed to anyone who can reach the port.
rules.remediation: Require authentication on the admin path, restrict it to a management network, or remove it from the exposed listener.

rules.title: Directory listing enabled
rules.why: A browsable directory index reveals file names, backups and structure that were never meant to be public.
rules.remediation: Disable autoindex / directory listing, or place an explicit index page in every served directory.

rules.title: Service inventory
rules.why: Open ports and identified services recorded for the report, not a vulnerability by itself.
rules.remediation: Confirm every open port is intentional; close anything that is not part of the documented service.
